description: Israel's final wilderness encampment, on the plains east of the Jordan opposite Jericho, where Balaam was hired to curse Israel and failed (Numbers 22-24), where Israelite men were drawn into idolatry and immorality with Moabite women at Baal-peor (Numbers 25), and where Moses delivered the sermons recorded in Deuteronomy before climbing Mount Nebo to view the promised land and die there (Deuteronomy 34:1-8).
family_friendly_summary: The Plains of Moab were Israel's last camp before entering the promised land, just east of the Jordan River across from Jericho. There a man named Balaam was hired to curse Israel but could only bless them. It was also where Moses gave his final speeches, written down in Deuteronomy, before climbing Mount Nebo to see the land and die.
